title: FBI crime database (NCIC) intrusion, reported Nov 20, 2026
disclaimer: Made for entertainment using AI. Not endorsed by the FBI, any government agency, news outlet, company, or anyone else named.
size_basis: NCIC is used by more than 100,000 criminal justice partners nationwide. No source says what was reached, so this is the worst case, not a known impact.
who_is_affected: Potentially police and courts that rely on NCIC, and people with records in it. No source says whose records, if any, were reached, and there is no notice for the public to act on.

known.text: CNN, NBC News, AP, ABC News, MS NOW and Fox News, each citing their own unnamed sources, report the FBI is investigating an apparent breach of NCIC.
NCIC is the FBI-run database police nationwide use for warrants, stolen property and other records.
The FBI has issued no statement. Asked on Nov 24, its Director said only that the matter is an ongoing investigation.
the President called the reported hack 'not good' on Nov 21 but gave no details.
The Director of National Intelligence said on Nov 22 the FBI 'has an incident' it is handling, without details.
A separate breach hit the FBI jobs site in September; the FBI blamed a contractor's missed patch.

not_known.text: Whether the FBI confirms the breach. The reports rest on unnamed sources, and the President, the DNI and the FBI Director gave no details.
What part of NCIC was reached, how the intruders got in, and who they are.
Whether any records were copied or changed.
Whether it is linked to this week's outages, the September jobs-site breach or the separate CIA and ODNI breach reported on Nov 24. No source says so.
Whether NCIC service for police was interrupted.
